Map sources and coverage

State outline and district boundaries from geoBoundaries. The simplified state outline is from 2011 (DataMeet India community and Election Commission of India, CC BY 2.5 India). District boundaries use the 2021 snapshot (Pathways Data and the Local Government Directory, ODbL). Use the live street map for current mapped geography.

Street map by OpenFreeMap. Walking and driving routes via FOSSGIS OSRM using OpenStreetMap data. Fix the map.

Nearby map features use an on-demand OpenStreetMap Overpass query. Mapped streetlights may be missing or out of service. Facility hours and staffing are unverified. Current weather is from Open-Meteo under CC BY 4.0.

Statewide routes show yellow where report evidence is unavailable. Use Trichy offline for report colours, GPS replay and saved walks in Central Trichy, Woraiyur, Manapparai, Srirangam and Thillai Nagar–Puthur.

SOS and motion drill

Arm motion detection while the page is open. A strong shake opens the SOS panel for confirmation. Use the drill during the exhibition.

What to look out for

    How the colours work

    Red shows one or more recent concerns without positive reports. Green requires two positive reports from separate report bundles and zero concerns. Yellow covers missing, stale, single positive or conflicting reports. Only reports matching the selected time window and dated within the last 14 days affect the colour. The custom window uses exact observation times in IST. Older bundles with only day/evening labels still work with those broad filters. Reports are unverified and the colours cannot establish whether a street is safe.

    Review a stretch

    Add an observation about the selected segment. Reports are stored in this browser. Import a report bundle from another participant to compare observations.

    Arrival check-in

    —

    Start a local timer for the estimated walk plus five minutes. Keep this tab open.

    The timer runs in this page and sends no messages.

    Nearby public landmarks

    Mapped places near the route. Opening hours and assistance availability are unverified.

      Map data and coverage

      OpenStreetMap snapshot dated 24 Nov 2026. This extract covers the selected offline area. Routes snap to the mapped walking network, which may omit paths, temporary closures and on-the-ground access restrictions.

      Physical setup

      One Arduino Uno R3 links the help point, motorised sign and staff desk.

      Help point

      HELP / GUIDE
      D2 / D3
      Amber / green LEDs
      D6 / D8

      Staff desk

      ACK / CLEAR
      D4 / D5
      Red LED / passive piezo
      D7 / D11

      Moving sign and path

      Servo signal
      D9
      White path LED
      D10
      Power, wiring and USB instructions

      Power the Uno by USB and the servo from a separate regulated 5 V supply rated at 1 A or more. Join the grounds. Use a 330 Ω series resistor with each LED and a 100 Ω resistor with the passive piezo. Connect the other side of each button to ground.

      For USB control, upload SafeLink_USB.ino to the Uno, close Arduino IDE’s Serial Monitor and choose Connect Arduino in a desktop browser with Web Serial support. The browser waits for the board to report its state at 115200 baud.

      SafeLink Station · Tabletop prototype. Alerts stay within the demonstration.
